detailed_description: File Hash reads a selected file in the browser and produces hexadecimal digests using the Web Crypto API. Click the dropzone to pick a file, then the tool reads it via arrayBuffer() and computes SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512 in parallel via crypto.subtle.digest. Because the Web Crypto API does not provide MD5, the MD5 row shows the first 32 characters of the SHA-256 hash and is labelled as 'SHA-256 truncated' rather than a real MD5 digest. The file name and a human-readable size are shown, and each hash has a Copy button. There is no drag-and-drop, algorithm toggle, batch hashing, JSON export, or comparison against an expected value.
usage_steps: Click the dropzone and select a file in the file picker
Wait for the loading indicator while the browser computes SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512
Review the file name and size shown in the info panel
Read the resulting hash values listed for MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512
Note that the MD5 row is the first 32 chars of the SHA-256 hash, marked 'SHA-256 truncated'
Click Copy on a row to copy that hash value to the clipboard
usage_examples: Compare a downloaded ISO's SHA-256 to the value published on a release page
Quickly grab the SHA-512 of a build artifact to paste into release notes
Confirm two copies of a file match by hashing each and comparing the SHA-256 values
Look up a file's SHA-1 for a tooling pipeline without installing a local hashing command
